title: 'Takot yan?': VP Duterte doesn't talk, act like someone who is in fear, says Adiong
summary: House Assistant Majority Lanao del Sur 1st district Rep. Zia Alonto Adiong says Vice President Sara Duterte doesn't appear to be fearing for her life, as she has claimed, based on her known demeanor.…

blocks.text: House Assistant Majority Lanao del Sur 1st district Rep. Zia Alonto Adiong says Vice President Sara Duterte doesn't appear to be fearing for her life, as she has claimed, based on her known demeanor.

This, as Adiong chided Duterte for playing the victim card after being issued an arrest warrant for three counts of grave threats, which stemmed from claims of planning to assassinate President Marcos and other members of the First Family.
The Vice President’s ordeal prompted her to declare over the weekend, "I do not feel safe. Pakiramdam ko papatayin nila [pulis] ako (I feel the police is out to kill me).
"I have documented threats and harrassment since 2023. I fear for my children. I do not feel they are safe if I am with them," she also said.
But Adiong doesn't buy Duterte’s fearful facade one bit.
“Kung titignan niyo, hindi po ito yung taong takot (If you look at her, she does not appear to be someone who is afraid). Actually, in fact, it’s the other way around,” he said.

He also pointed to Duterte’s previous public statements that he said appeared to invoke violence against President Marcos, as well as her continued requests for travel clearance, as inconsistent with her claim that she had been under threat since 2023.

“Siya yung nagbibigay ng mga statement na nagpapahiwatig ng violence against the President, pupugutan ng ulo (She was the one making statements suggesting violence against the President, including that he would be beheaded)... So it’s not an indication of someone who’s been receiving threats,” he said.
These notwithstanding, Adiong stressed that any threat against Duterte should be taken seriously and properly investigated by authorities.
He said the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) had given her an opportunity to submit information about the threats she claimed to have received, but no such information had been provided.

“They were given the chance. They were called, invited by the NBI na isubmit po nila kung ano po yung threats na ... natatanggap nila (They were called and invited by the NBI to submit information about the threats they had received.
“Pero hanggang ngayon, wala po silang naibibigay (But until now, they have not provided anything)," Adiong noted.

Seemingly referring to Duterte’s subsequent criticisms on the court and police, the Mindanao congressman stressed that public officials should respect the courts and the law even when proceedings or their outcomes are unfavorable to them.

“In this case, whether or not favorable sa’yo, kailangan mo talaga as an elected official to prove to the people that we have our laws, we have to respect our laws, and only through our laws and through our courts can we defend ourselves."

(In this case, whether or not it is favorable to you, as an elected official you have to prove to the people that we have laws, that we have to respect them, and that only through our laws and courts can we defend ourselves.)
The law applies to everyone

For Adiong, the grave threats case demonstrates that the law applies equally to everyone regardless of status or position, rejecting claims from Duterte’s camp and supporters that the proceedings constitute political persecution.

“Ito pong nangyayari ngayon, ito po ang nagpapatunay na gumugulong po ang hustisya sa ating bansa. Wala pong tinitingnan na status or posisyon ng isang tao pagdating sa pananagutan at sa pag-implement ng mga patakaran o ating batas,” he said.

(What is happening now proves that justice is taking its course in our country. No one’s status or position is considered when it comes to accountability and the implementation of our rules and laws.)
He said the criminal case should also be distinguished from Duterte’s ongoing impeachment proceedings.
“Magkaiba naman po yung mga hukom na tumatayo dito at yung magiging verdict po ay magkaiba (The judges handling these cases are different, and the verdicts will also be different)."
